name: Hill Swallow
rangeDescription: Southern india and sri lanka
description: A small dark blue-black swallow with rufous-chestnut on its face and a short tail. Except for a black triangular eye-stripe extending to the bill, the entire forehead, chin, throat, and upper breast are rufous-chestnut, without any dark necklace like that of Barn Swallow, the main confusion species.

name: Snares Penguin
rangeDescription: Snares islands and adjacent waters off new zealand
description: Medium-sized crested penguin, endemic to New Zealand. Note the thin, vivid yellow eyebrow that droops behind the eye to form a bushy tufted crest.

name: Large-tailed Antshrike
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (minas gerais) to eastern paraguay and far northeastern argentina
description: Medium-sized antshrike with a rather small head, a short robust bill, and a long tail. Males are black with white spots and an entirely black tail while females are black with cinnamon spots and barring throughout.

name: Talaud Bush-hen
rangeDescription: Talaud islands (northern moluccas)
description: A large, entirely dark, pale-billed rail confined to the Talaud Archipelago. Upperparts and head dark brown, underparts completely slate-colored.

name: Calabarzon Babbler
rangeDescription: Philippines (southern sierra madre mountains of southern luzon)
description: A fairly small bird of lowland and foothill forest and edge; endemic to Luzon, though lumped with Visayan Babbler under “Black-crowned Babbler” by some taxonomies. Has a gray back and cheek with fine pale streaks, dark wings and tail with white outer tail feathers, white underparts, a pale rufous throat, and a black crown.

name: Bearded Guan
rangeDescription: Andes of southern ecuador (but not the east slope) and western andes of northwestern peru
description: Large chickenlike bird with a long tail. Chocolate-brown overall with pinkish-red legs and silvery frosting on head and neck.

name: Styan's Bulbul
rangeDescription: Coastal lowland forest of eastern and southern taiwan
description: Relatively plain songbird, olive above, whitish below, with black cap, white face, and black moustachial mark. Somewhat similar to more widespread Light-vented Bulbul, with which it hybridizes, but adult Styan’s has heavier bill, solidly black cap, white plumage surrounding the eye, and small red dot in black moustachial stripe (difficult to see).

name: Bay-capped Wren-Spinetail
rangeDescription: Far southern brazil to uruguay and central argentina
description: Small, with a long spiky tail. Has a brown-streaked black back contrasting with a cinnamon crown and pale underparts.

name: Atlantic Royal Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (minas gerais, rio de janeiro, são paulo, and paraná)
description: Endemic to southeastern Brazil. Uncommon, medium-sized, overall brown flycatcher of humid tropical forest in lowlands.

name: Socotra Buzzard
rangeDescription: Socotra (off eastern somalia)
description: A typical medium-sized brown-and-white buzzard that was only recognized as distinct in 2010. The underparts are whitish buff with heavily streaked underparts (lighter on the throat).

name: Northern Screamer
rangeDescription: Northern colombia and northwestern venezuela
description: Huge, ungainly bird with thick red legs, red face, and a wispy crest. Body mostly gray with black neck and whitish cheeks.

name: Shining Drongo
rangeDescription: Forest of guinea and sierra leone to gabon and eastern democratic republic of the congo
description: A large, extremely glossy square-tailed drongo of forest understory, often found with mixed-species flocks. Habitat is this species’ most reliable field mark, as no other drongos are regularly found in forest understory.

name: Black-faced Solitaire
rangeDescription: Mountains of costa rica and western panama (east to veraguas)
description: Sleek medium-sized thrush with a beautiful voice. Listen for its fluty, ethereal phrases drifting over montane forests.

name: Blue Mountain Vireo
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of northwestern jamaica
description: A stout, plain vireo of woodlands with dense foliage, preferring higher elevation and wetter forests. This species lacks facial markings or wingbars of other Caribbean vireos.

name: Sulphur-throated Finch
rangeDescription: Arid littoral of southwestern ecuador and northwestern peru
description: Drab and nomadic finch-like bird found in desert and arid scrub in northwestern Peru and southwestern Ecuador. While some birds show a distinct yellowish wash on their face and throat and a short mustache, many individuals lack these features, and easily could be confused with female Parrot-billed Seedeater.

name: New Hanover Munia
rangeDescription: New hanover (northeastern bismarck archipelago)
description: A small, little-known bird of grasslands and clearings on New Hanover in the Bismarck islands. Black underparts, back and face, brown wings, yellow rump and tail, and a silver-gray bill.

name: Plumbeous Ibis
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southern brazil to bolivia, paraguay, and northeastern argentina
description: Distinctive gray ibis with a white forehead and bushy crest. Favors marshes, rice fields, and ponds, but also occurs in grassland, pastures, and savanna.

name: Short-tailed Field Tyrant
rangeDescription: Arid southwestern ecuador to far northern chile; gorgona island (colombia)
description: A small, oddly-shaped flycatcher that inhabits deserts and other arid habitats. It is found mainly west of the Andes, but ranges up into interior valleys in a few areas.

name: Puna Yellow-Finch
rangeDescription: Andes of southern peru (cusco) to western bolivia and northwestern argentina
description: Rather local but sometimes numerous in the high Andes. Favors puna grasslands, stony plains with shrubby bushes, villages, and bogs.

name: Bonaparte's Gull
rangeDescription: Northern north america; winters to mexico and greater antilles
description: The most common small gull through most of North America, especially inland. Breeding adults have a black head, thin white eye arcs, bright red legs, light gray upperparts, and black wingtips.
